Assuming minimal hardening of the material post-yield (a reasonable assumption for pipe steel), collapse would then be imminent given any non-symmetry in the loading. For below-ground pipes, additional terms are added to include hydrostatic pressure of the soil loading. Note that water saturation of the surrounding soil can add additional pressure loading to the pipe; this has been neglected for convenience. Also, cohesive forces in the soil can help diffuse or support some portion of the loading. However, these terms are dependent on soil parameters for which we do not have good estimates, thus this term was neglected. Soil parameters are considered in more detail in the ring deformation collapse case in section 2.2. Ring deformation collapse (buckling) In this case, failure occurs when loading causes ovalling of the pipe to the extent that the pipe reaches structural instability and collapses. This criterion is valid for both above and below-ground pipes but has different expressions for these cases. The expressions for below-ground pipes add additional terms related to soil strength, which can assist in resisting ovalling, and in the weight of the soil, which accentuates ovalling.
